hero.h1: Tankless Water Heaters in Evanston, IL
hero.sub: Endless hot water and a heater that hangs on the wall. We install, repair and descale tankless water heaters in Evanston, and we'll tell you honestly whether one makes sense for your home. Our Evanston office is on Orrington Avenue, downtown.

img.alt: Plumber working on the copper water lines of a wall-mounted tankless water heater in a basement

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: A tankless heater fires only when a hot tap opens. Water flows through a heat exchanger and comes out hot for as long as you need it. Each unit has a flow limit, so we size it for the most hot water your home uses at once.

blocks.h2: Is Tankless Right for Your Evanston Home?
blocks.intro: A few local factors decide it.

items.body: At about 7.8 grains per gallon, a yearly descaling keeps it running well.
Tankless units vent through a wall, not the chimney.
Older gas piping may need to be upsized.
Check with your association about exterior vents.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.body: A tankless heater has a narrow heat exchanger, and minerals in hard water can build up inside it. With Evanston's hard water, that means descaling about once a year to keep the unit efficient and protect the warranty. Many homeowners pair a tankless heater with a water softener or a scale-reduction filter. We'll explain the options and set you up with a maintenance schedule when we install it.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a Tankless Install
blocks.body: Gas line size and venting are the two big variables. Older homes often need a larger gas line to the heater and a new vent through an outside wall. Removing the old tank and adding isolation valves for descaling are part of the job. We check everything first and quote one flat price.

items.q: How often does a tankless heater need descaling in Evanston?
items.answer: About once a year with Evanston's water. A softener can stretch that.

items.q: Can a tankless heater vent through my chimney?
items.answer: No. It needs its own vent, usually through a side wall.

items.q: Will I really get endless hot water?
items.answer: Yes, as long as you don't ask for more hot water at once than it's sized for.
Yes. We descale, clean sensors and replace failed parts.

items.q: Will a tankless heater lower my gas bill?
items.answer: Often, because it doesn't keep a tank of water hot all day. Savings depend on your use.
